findings.claim: Original 00409210 tests abs(signed32_cross) < max(abs(signed32_dx),abs(signed32_dy)) with strict inequality and int32 wrap; class zero includes degenerate segments and exact tolerance-boundary points.
findings.limitations: Signed-int32 overflow/INT_MIN behavior is specific to i386; do not generalize to unbounded integer arithmetic.

findings.claim: For nondegenerate ordinary coordinates, class 1 denotes before first lateral cross-section endpoint, 2 denotes between inclusive endpoints, and 3 beyond second; class 0 is outside the ribbon. All branches tested in original-instruction emulation.
findings.limitations: Exact native axis-comparison precedence must be preserved for unusual overflow or degenerate coordinates.

findings.claim: Read-only original I76EDIT.EXE x86 P-code emulation performed 896 deterministic samples, with no execution failures and no discrepancies against independent signed-int32 model; 24 native opcode checks passed.
findings.limitations: Instruction-level original-code emulation only; no full Windows editor or exported terrain was exercised.

findings.claim: Original 00421DF0 uses half-normal times 5 for modes 1-3 and half-normal times plus/minus 2 for modes 4-5, corresponding to approximate 5-unit and 2-unit nominal lateral raster section widths for observed unit input.
findings.limitations: Final pixel extents also depend on original float truncation, raster iteration, and mode/classifier gating; not the visible RSEG width.

findings.claim: Helper 004235A4 truncates x87 to signed integer; selected 00421DF0 coordinate conversions adjust only when signed trunc(x*10) modulo 10 is greater than 4, making the additional rounding branch asymmetric for negative values.
findings.limitations: Native branch semantics established, but complete bit-level float32/x87 tie boundary and negative world-coordinate authoring validity are unresolved.
